## Motivation The SM107 custom all-reduce table (#36397) was tuned before `2shot_push` existed. #42811 added `2shot_push` later but retuned only the SM100 rows, so SM107 never enables it. Above the 1shot_push ceiling, SM107 sizes fall through to `2shot_pull` (TP4 graph) or multicast `2shot_pull` (TP4 eager, TP8, TP16). On SM107, a per-algorithm sweep shows `2shot_push` is the fastest custom algorithm from about 1 MB (TP4), 384 KB (TP8) and 256 KB (TP16) up to 16 MB. Every other threshold in the #36397 table lines up with the sweep to within one size step. ## Modifications `_sm107_configs` (`configs/custom_all_reduce_v2.py`) only: - `config()` takes an optional `two_shot_push=` threshold, the same keyword the SM100 table uses. It defaults to 0 (disabled), so worlds that don't set it are unchanged. - **TP4**: 1shot ceiling 6.938 MB (graph) / 9.812 MB (eager) becomes 1 MB, then `2shot_push` up to 16 MB. The eager multicast range is untouched; it is only reached above 16 MB. - **TP8**: 1shot ceiling 2.438 MB becomes 384 KB, then `2shot_push` up to 16 MB. - **TP16**: 1shot ceiling 832 KB becomes 256 KB, then `2shot_push` up to 16 MB. - **TP2** is unchanged: `2shot_push` never wins there. TP3/5/6/7 are not tuned and keep their #36397 rows. `test_custom_all_reduce.py::test_custom_all_reduce_eager_plan_follows_config` zeroes every threshold to force the NCCL path. It now also zeroes `two_shot_push_threshold`; otherwise the size still routes to `2shot_push` on any arch whose table enables it. ## Accuracy Tests `test/registered/kernels/ops/communication/test_custom_all_reduce.py` (bit-exact against NCCL, graph and eager) on SM107: | world | result | |---|---| | 2 | 310 passed | | 4 | 310 passed | | 8 (2 nodes, MNNVL) | 310 passed (every rank) | | 16 (4 nodes, MNNVL) | 310 passed (every rank) | ## Speed Tests and Profiling The method follows #42811: - bf16 input. - One CUDA graph of 100 back-to-back all-reduces; median of 9 replays; max over ranks. - Eager mode is the eager dispatch path captured without `comm.capture()`, so staging copies are included and Python launch overhead is not. - Ranks are aligned on the GPU (a tiny NCCL all-reduce) right before each timed replay. - Per-algorithm columns are forced through `override_algo`; multicast `2shot_pull` is forced with a temporary heuristic. - "today" and "this PR" are the tuned tables run end to end (`auto`).
